citation.description: Ticket Approach section explicitly records the decision: 'When one holder outlives the whole budget every waiter fails regardless of service order, so FIFO buys nothing here. Bounded re-attempts convert loss into latency with less machinery than a queue.'

criteria.criterion: The retry-vs-fair-queueing decision is recorded in Approach with its selecting evidence.
A write whose first budget expires is re-attempted, verified by pytest -q tests/unit/test_lock_retry_zebrafish.py -k reproduction exiting 0.
The retry never replays the write body, verified by the no-double-append test asserting an appended-event count of exactly 1.
A write exhausting every pass raises LockTimeout naming the cumulative wait, verified by the exhaustion test's message assertion.
`claim` succeeds on a later pass behind an over-budget holder, verified by the claim-path test.
`claim`'s error text carries the cumulative wait, verified by asserting the CommandError message contains it.
`claim`'s error text names the holder, verified by asserting the CommandError message contains the holder string.
Opted-in sites are exactly five, distributed 3/1/1, verified by AST-based test.
The advisory push.py:361 merge stays fail-fast, verified by the fail-fast test asserting that acquire is called with retries=0 on that path.
Each exhausted pass logs a warning naming the holder, verified by a caplog test asserting one record per exhausted pass.
The `retries` default is 0 so unedited callers are unchanged, verified by a test asserting inspect.signature(lock.acquire).parameters['retries'].default == 0.
`REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES=0` restores fail-fast, verified by the env-override test.
Out-of-range `REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES` clamps to [0,10], verified by the clamp test.
`docs/concurrency.md` documents the ~180s ceiling.
`docs/concurrency.md` documents the override (REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES).
